e2.store: sqlite (SqliteSaver, WAL, file on local disk), durability='sync' (most durable built-in mode)

W1.manual_intervention: none (graph.invoke(None, config) in a fresh process)
W1.notes: Kill at charge entry before its ledger write; the agent step that chose charge was checkpointed. Resume re-runs the tools node once.

W2.manual_intervention: none (graph.invoke(None, config) in a fresh process)
W2.notes: Kill after the charge ledger fsync, before return. The tools node never finished, so nothing about it was recorded; resume re-runs the whole node -> second charge. Both ledger lines carry the same task_id and tool_call_id: a stable key is derivable but LangGraph does not forward or check one.

W3.manual_intervention: none (graph.invoke(None, config) in a fresh process)
W3.notes: Kill right after the tools task's pending write (charge ToolMessage) committed. Pending write (or the already-saved superstep checkpoint) is reapplied; the tools node is not re-run.

W3b.manual_intervention: none (graph.invoke(None, config) in a fresh process)
W3b.notes: Kill at the start of model call 3, after the superstep checkpoint. Resume re-runs only the agent node.

W4.manual_intervention: none (graph.invoke(None, config) in a fresh process)
W4.notes: Kill inside SqliteSaver.put for the checkpoint that carries the charge result (statements executed, transaction uncommitted). NOT deterministic in outcome even though the kill point is: the tools task's put_writes is submitted to a thread pool and is not ordered before the checkpoint put; when put won the lock first, the charge result was in neither table -> tools node re-run -> duplicate (2/5).

W4b.manual_intervention: none (graph.invoke(None, config) in a fresh process)
W4b.notes: Kill inside put_writes of the charge result, before commit. Result lost; resume re-runs the tools node -> duplicate.

W5.notes: Kill right after triage's Command(goto='specialist') write committed. Fresh process: next=['specialist']; specialist re-ran from its start with the same task_id (its in-flight model call 1 was repeated: it had not been recorded).

W6.manual_intervention: a person supplies Command(resume={'approve': True}) (by design)
W6.notes: SIGKILL while suspended in interrupt(). Fresh process sees next=['approval'] and the interrupt id/value; approval node re-executes from its start and interrupt() returns the resume value. A second identical Command(resume) after completion was a no-op (charges stay 1).

durability_exit.note: exit mode writes nothing until the run exits; after SIGKILL there is no checkpoint, invoke(None) raises EmptyInputError (all progress lost, effectively lost_progress). W3/W4b hooks never fire in exit mode (no put_writes during the run), so those runs completed un-killed and are not_applicable.

concurrent_resume_no_fence.note: After a W1 crash, two fresh processes resumed the same thread; no owner/lease/fence exists, both executed charge (same task_id). Final state shows 1 charge ToolMessage vs 2 in the ledger.

e3.flow: triage --Command(goto='specialist')--> specialist --(charge proposed)--> approval node [interrupt()] --> ToolNode --> specialist
e3.context_passed: full shared state: the `messages` channel (add_messages reducer) is the same list for every node; specialist saw 3 messages (human, triage AI tool-call, transfer ToolMessage). Filtering/summaries are app code.
e3.state_owner: the graph run (Pregel loop) owns state; nodes only return writes; the checkpointer stores it keyed by thread_id/checkpoint_ns/checkpoint_id. `active_agent` is an app-level field.
e3.execution_ids: thread_id (caller-chosen), checkpoint_id (uuid6 per superstep), task_id (deterministic hash of checkpoint id+ns+step+node+trigger; identical when a task is re-executed after a crash), interrupt id (xxh3 of checkpoint_ns), tool_call_id (from the model).

specialist_fails_no_retry.notes: invoke raised RuntimeError; error stored as pending ERROR write (get_state().tasks[].error); next=['specialist']; a fresh process invoke(None) re-ran specialist (same task_id) and continued.

specialist_fails_with_retry.notes: RetryPolicy(max_attempts=2): attempt 2 in-process, same task_id, execution_info.node_attempt=2. Retry state is not persisted across processes.

e5.task: E1 (3 scripted model calls, 2 tool calls; ledger fsync per tool call included in all variants)
e5.durable_store: SqliteSaver on local file, WAL (set by SqliteSaver.setup), durability=sync
